rule.name: LoopUpdateAwayFromExit
rule.message: This for loop moves its index away from its own exit condition: the condition keeps holding while the update runs the other way (i >= 0 with i++, i < n with i--, i <= 0 with i--), so the loop never ends and fails with an IndexOutOfBoundsException or runs until the index overflows. Count in the direction the condition tests: for (int i = list.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--) and for (int i = 0; i < n; i++). Right code is not reported: a loop that leaves through break, return or throw on another condition, a loop that assigns the index in its body, and a byte, short or char index that wraps on purpose.
